OWNER SPECIFICATION REVIEW EVENT, r11 Part A (the ten-row owner packet), 2026-09-16.
Recorded under the r11 closure mandate's AFK review authority on an explicit owner ruling,
transcribed verbatim in work/r11-campaign/RULINGS-OWNER-10.md. This is a CLAIM CORRECTION:
the registry is brought to what the code already does, and no implementation was weakened.

RULING (row 2, R11-593, filed high / adjudicated medium): OPTION A. Do NOT reopen live
trust-anchor rotation merely to make the old theorem prose true.

WHAT MOVED: `statement`, `security_consequence` and `scope`.

WHY THE OLD TEXT WAS FALSE. It claimed "a rebuild with withdrawn trust advances the epoch and
stops resumption". Anchors are immutable for a listener's lifetime, and `bind_resumption`
hands `republish` the epoch the store already holds (tls_listener_state/mod.rs:218-221), so
`SharedTlsAuthEpoch::store` always returns `None` and the change branch never fires on any
build path. The registered control called `EpochBoundSessionStore::republish` DIRECTLY with a
different anchor set (auth_epoch.rs:399-407) — a store-level capability no listener path
reaches — and no control in the packet would have failed had `republish` been deleted from
`bind_resumption` entirely. The claim also contradicted its own premise: THM-0103's scope
already says this theorem "must never be read as establishing that a production listener's
epoch ADVANCES when its anchors change, which nothing in the tree establishes", and the
owner's module table warns "Proposition 1 must never be read as evidence for proposition 2."

WHY OPTION A. ADR-MCPRE-062, superseding ADR-MCPRE-055 (#598), chose the immutable-listener
replacement/restart model deliberately, and the code implements that choice. Making the code
match the prose would have reopened live anchor rotation to satisfy a sentence.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM. The statement now says a replacement listener and session-cache boundary
does not carry resumption authority across the replacement when the epoch differs: a
different anchor set is a different state with its own empty cache, while a rebuild that
republishes the same trust keeps its cache. The consequence is bounded to ACROSS THE
REPLACEMENT — true under the replacement model and false if read as covering a live listener.
The scope states explicitly that nothing here establishes a live listener's epoch advancing,
names cache NON-CONTINUITY as the real safety property, and records the operator obligation:
changing the trust-anchor set requires listener replacement or restart for the new trust
epoch to become authoritative. That obligation is stated and proved by nothing, and a reader
must not take this claim as relieving it.

THE EVIDENCE RULING. The control was renamed to
`republishing_a_different_epoch_supersedes_the_stores_sessions` and carries a note saying it
is a claim about the STORE — THM-0103's subject — and about no listener. `proxy.tls_listener_state`
supports both theorems, so the name is the mechanism that keeps the two propositions apart;
a control must not be left standing as evidence for a claim whose production path it cannot
observe.
